full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J: These appeals by leave are by the pre-emptee against the common judgment in Civil Revision Nos. 567 and 568 of 1990 of a single Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rules. The Civil Revisions were filed against the judgment and order dated January 24, 1990 in Miscellaneous Appeal Nos. 120 and 121 of 1987 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka affirming the judgment and order dated April 23, 1987 of the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 189 and 190 of 1984 allowing the same. The Miscellaneous Cases were filed under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 1949 seeking preemption in respect of the land in Dhanmondi Residential Area (Dhanmondi R/A). 

 4. The Miscellaneous Cases were opposed by the appellant and another (Respondent  No. 2) by filing written objection contending inter alia, that in respect of the land transferred in the year 1984 there were agreements of the year 1977 between the vendor and the vendees and that the pre-emptor had knowledge about the sale long before 17.8.1984. It was also contended by the pre-emptee that miscellaneous cases were barred by limitation and that some were not maintainable because of the provision 01' section of 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 5. The trial Court allowed the prayer for pre-emption on the finding that Miscellaneous cases were not barred by limitation and that also not barred tinder the provision of section 85(2) of the Non-Agricultural and Tenancy Act. 1949. The pre-emptee-Appellant went on appeal against the judgment and order of the Court of Assistant Judge before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. The Miscellaneous Appeal were heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka and he dismissed the appeals. 

 6. The preemptee-appellant thereafter moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rules in the Civil Revisions discharged the Rules on the finding "the land was acquired by the Government only to develop demarcate plots and lease out to interested persons retaining its superior right in respect of transfer correction of record, fixing of rent or subsequent enhancement of rent or any other terms on expiry of the lease of 99 years but by this Government does not create obstacle in the beneficial enjoyment of the property its transferability and inheritance by the descendants but the transferability will he always controlled on principle that the land as far as possible should he retained by the heirs of lessee under principles and policy of the pre-emption law. Therefore, I hold that preemption under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act is very much applicable to the Dhanmondi Residential plot sold to others by the co-sharers". 

 7. Leave was granted to consider the contention of the appellant as in view of the provision of Sub-section 1(c) of section 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 as well as in view of the discussion in the of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 as well as in view of the discussion in the case of Md. Mosaddeque Hossain Vs. Dr. Esmat Mirza and others reported in 18 BID (AD) 57 pre-emption sought under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 was not maintainable the High Court Division was in error in discharging the Rule and not holding that pre-emption was not available under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act as against the transfer to the pre-emptee-appellant by the co-sharers of the land of plot No. 543/A in Road No. 13 of Dhanmondi R/A . 

 8. The learned Counsel for the appellant primarily argued in the background of the decision of this court in the case reported in 18 BLD (AD) 57 as to the maintainability of the Miscellaneous cases tiled under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act as regard non-agricultural land in Dhanmondi R/A. 

 9. The question similar to the question involved in the present appeals came up for consideration before this court in the case mentioned hereinabove This court upon considering the provisions of section 85(2) of Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act,1949 which reads as:- 

 Provided that the right vested in a tenant by the provisions of this Act shall not be divested by the acquisition of the superior right only in the land by the Government." and the provision of section 81 A (2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 which reads as" His rights and liabilities of other non-agricultural tenants shall except in the matter of determination, enhancement or reduction of rent, be governed by the terms of the lease and the provisions of the Transfer of the Property Act, 1882 (Act IV of 1882)" (provisio to the subsection is not relevant for the present purpose) has held   that the object of section 85(2) of the Act was to retain control over non-agricultural land held by a tenant under the Government unencumbered by the provisions of the NAT Act. Section 81A(2) stated positively how the rights and liabilities of non-agricultural tenants other that those who have become tenants under the Government by virtue of compulsory acquisition of land shall he determined. The NAT Act has not been mentioned to be a governing law in respect of such tenants of non-agricultural land under the Government. Hence on both accounts, under section 85(2) of the NAT Act and section 81A (2) of the SAT Act the ouster of NAT Act film) the categories mentioned therein are complete. Section 24 of the NAT Act has no manner of application to lands of Dhanmondi Residential Area". 

 10. The learned Counsel for the Respondent No. 1 made submissions amongst other that prayer for pre-emption was very much maintainable since the land sought to be preempted was not acquired for the use of the Government directly or for any office or Department of the Government but for the use of the lessees of the Government which in no way can he considered that the land so acquired is being used by the Government or by any office or Department of the Government and that denying of right of pre-emption in respect of the land or Dhanmondi Residential Area which is non-agricultural land but exercise of right of pre-emption in respect of other non-agricultural land while available under the provision of section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy. Act would result in discrimination as regard the right of pre-emption amongst the non-agricultural tenants. This particular contention of the learned Counsel for the respondent in our view is not well funded in law in that in barring pre-emption in respect of the land of Dhanmondi Residential Area upon resorting to the provision of section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act no discrimination has been made in between the tenants of the said residential area. The tenants of the other non-agricultural land are being in the different category the bar of pre-emption as has been made as to land of Dhanmondi. R/A. cannot he said discrimination in any respect amongst the class of non-agricultural tenants in general The bar as to pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is limited amongst the tenants of Non- Agricultural land in Dhanmondi R/A and thereby no discrimination has been done amongst the non-agricultural tenants of the said particular area, rather the tenants of the said limited are has been treated equally. The bar so made as to pre-emption of the land of Dhanmondi, R.A. appears to be rational and does not offend the rule of non-discrimination amongst the same class of person placed in the same situation. The other contention that the land sought to be pre-empted as is not used by the Government or by any office or Department of the Government cannot he said immune iron being pre-empted under section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act also not well funded in law because of the fact that the land sought to be pre-empted is being held by the lessee-tenants under the Government in respect of acquisitioned land being same leased out. Provision of sub-section 2 of section 85 of NAT Act clearly shows that provision of section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act shall not he applicable in respect of non-agricultural land as mentioned in section 85(1) of NAT Act and that land of Dhanmondi R/A being the land of one of those categories as the same is held by special kind of tenant of the Government pre-emption is not available. There is no dispute that the lands in Dhanmondi Residential Area are non-agricultural land and the same are being held by the lessees as being the tenants under the Government. Proviso to sub-section (2) of section 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, and the sub-section (I) of section 81 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 clearly show that non-agricultural tenants who have become tenants under the Government by virtue of acquisition of the superior right in non-agricultural land by the provision of SAT Act the provisions of Nat Act, if so were application to such tenants at the time of acquisition would be regulated by the provision of NAT Act. The application by section 24 NAT Act has been excluded by the provision of section 85(2) of NAT Act in respect of the land mentioned in section 85 (1) (a,b,c,d,e) and land of Dhanmondi R.A being the land of one of the category of lands as in section 85(1) (a,b,c,d,e) application of provision of section 24 NAT Act has been excluded by section 85(2) NAT Act. 

 12. Since the point involved in the appeals is as to whether lands in Dhanmondi Residential Area are or not subject to pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and as the said point is covered by the decision in the case reported in 18 BLD (AD) 57 and that as the decision in the reported case fully applicable to the facts as well as law involved in the appeals and that also to the points urged for consideration in the appeals we are of the view that in the afore state of the matter and also in the light of our discussions made herein over the judgment and decision of the High Court Division calls for interference.
